body:
Is this all being done in map frame? If the frame of the request is the same as that of the costmap, it should simply bypass https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/blob/30048b46bf02c6a60473b1dae6000e6eb2597056/nav2_costmap_2d/src/costmap_2d_ros.cpp#L588.

So an easy option that if you're not using map frame, is to convert your request to map frame initially (or change the global frame of the costmap to a different frame, I suppose)

> Is this all being done in map frame?

In my application, its easy enough for me to provide the goal in the map frame instead of a different one. However, I can imagine a case where a Nav2 user/developer would (as an example) want to provide a goal relative to the robot. They may then expect Nav2 to lock in that target goal at the beginning of path planning/following, instead of constantly transforming that goal back into the map frame (which would keep moving the goal). This could be accomplished outside of Nav2 by pre-transforming the goal before sending it to Nav2

Regardless of whether the above example is behavior that should be supported, I'd argue that passing in a pose with a fixed timestamp in a non-map frame should at least inform the developer (through a log message perhaps) that the goal will be continuously transformed. This functionality is different from how move_base in ROS1 navigation would handle it (see [move_base.cpp:658](https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation/blob/noetic-devel/move_base/src/move_base.cpp#L658)), where it looks like the goal is transformed once at the beginning, and only transformed further if the frame id changes due to a new goal being received.

> want to provide a goal relative to the robot

There's nothing preventing you from having the planner server operate in a different and robot-body relative frame, also would make it so that there's no TF transforms necessary to operate. 

> They may then expect Nav2 to lock in that target goal at the beginning of path planning/following, instead of constantly transforming that goal back into the map frame (which would keep moving the goal). 

That would be a false expectation. Frames move, and if you're trying to navigate relative to a time-variant frame, the expectation is that we're taking the most recent transformation to use or else you're navigating to a stale goal. Imagine you wanted your goal to be a frame representing a person moving through a scene, you could easily assign that person a frame from whatever detection mechanism you like and then plan to a point behind the person using that reference frame (to follow). If we didn't continuously transform, then this would not work.

If you don't have a time variant frame, then you can easily pre-transform that data and provide it in the planner servers' reference frame that you've selected for use in your configuration. There are many proposed solutions. Obviously if you want to build an arbitrary robotic system, you're going to need to configure the framework to meet the needs of it, but all of these solutions are possible and pretty trivial to implement by design since what you're doing is pretty typical.
